claims.claim: The x402 V2 and MPP HTTP-402 protocols differ in payloads, settlement, and infrastructure.

sources.quote: x402 defines PaymentRequirements, PaymentPayload, and facilitator verify and settle interfaces.
MPP Charge uses SEP-41 transfers; Channel uses a one-way channel with cumulative commitments.

claims.notes: The owner specifications expose different payloads, settlement paths, and components.

claims.claim: x402 V2 provides extensions and discovery.

sources.quote: Extensions enable modular optional functionality; GET /supported returns supported extensions; tags support discovery filtering.

claims.notes: The same specification states that session handling is out of scope.

claims.claim: MPP uses on-chain Charge settlement and cumulative off-chain Session channel commitments.

sources.quote: Each Charge payment settles on-chain individually; Channel signs cumulative off-chain commitments without per-payment transactions.

claims.notes: The current SDK calls the repeated-payment implementation Channel.

claims.claim: AP2/ACP cover above-rail authorization/mandate/audit and beta commerce, respectively.

sources.quote: AP2 defines Checkout and Payment Mandates, receipts, authorization evidence, and dispute evidence within a commerce protocol.
ACP remains beta and covers cart, feed, orders, authentication, payment handlers, and checkout.

claims.notes: AP2 operates within a commerce protocol. ACP delegates payment to handlers.

sources.quote: Current schemas and examples model checkout totals, payment handlers, fulfillment, Idempotency-Key behavior, orders, and refunds.
x402 separates payment requirements, payload, verification, settlement, and resource response.

claims.notes: This adapter boundary is an engineering synthesis across the distinct specifications.
